test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

He has **much works** to finish.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 - a lot of work**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"works"** is often used in the plural form to refer to productions or creations like literary works or artistic works. However, when referring to tasks or labor, the singular term **"work"** is used. (कार्य)

 
 
• **Example: **The works of Shakespeare are studied all over the world.
 
 
 
• **"a lot of work"** refers to a large amount of tasks or effort required to be done. (बहुत सारा काम)
 
 
• **Example: **He has a lot of work to finish before the deadline.
 
 
 
• Hence, the phrase "much works" is incorrect, and the correct replacement is "a lot of work."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 - a lot of work**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Plenty works** (बहुत सारे कार्य): This phrase is grammatically incorrect as "plenty" should be followed by singular nouns when referring to tasks or labor.

 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: She has plenty works to do. Correct: She has plenty of work to do.
 
 
 
• **Many works** (कई कार्य): While "many works" can refer to multiple creations or productions, it is not suitable to describe tasks or labor.
 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: He has many works to finish. Correct: He has many tasks to finish.
 
 
 
• **Lot of tasks** (बहुत सारे कार्य): While grammatically correct, this phrase changes the meaning of the sentence as it uses "tasks" instead of "work."
 
 
• **Example:** He has a lot of tasks to complete before the deadline.
 
 

16a:T7f4,
The correct answer is Option 2
